source_name: Prekoveze.me – employer-scoped job listings (e.g. Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka)
why_relevant: Aggregator with per-employer pages, letting the hiring history of each Montenegrin bank be tracked as a time series — role titles shifting toward 'implementacija' or a named platform is the weak signal this cell exists to catch.

source_name: Careerjet Montenegro – 'posao banka' aggregated feed
why_relevant: Cross-portal aggregator that surfaces bank vacancies which never reach the two main national boards; cheap broad net for hiring signals.

source_name: Bankar.me – 'Oglasi za posao' category (banking-sector vacancy news)
why_relevant: Montenegrin banking trade portal that republishes bank and Central Bank vacancy announcements as articles, so ads survive after the original posting expires — an archive of hiring signals. Also publishes a branch/ATM location overview useful for infrastructure baselining.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica – Aktuelni konkursi za zapošljavanje (careers)
why_relevant: Direct issuer-side vacancy page of a major Montenegrin bank; job titles and requirement lists frequently name the incumbent systems and the projects being staffed.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore – Karijera (careers page)
why_relevant: Issuer-side vacancy page of a domestically owned bank; observed to advertise payment-operations and multi-position rounds. Same site's 'Poslovna mreža' page enumerates branches/ATMs, a proxy for terminal-estate size.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) – cards & POS terminals pages
why_relevant: Largest acquirer in the market; its own product pages disclose estate scale (stated as over 4,000 POS terminals, network operating since 2002). Estate-size disclosures by acquirers are the demand-side counterpart to vendor installed-base claims and help time refresh cycles.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe – solutions and references
why_relevant: Regional market leader in banking software and parent of Payten; group site and local subsidiary structure (including a stake in E-Mon, Podgorica) reveal the Montenegrin delivery footprint. Product/reference pages hint at which banks run its stack (e.g. NLB Banka Podgorica mobile/e-banking apps built on Asseco platforms).

source_name: Google Play / app-store publisher and package metadata for Montenegrin bank apps
why_relevant: Android package identifiers leak the software supplier of each bank's channel: 'hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbcrnagoracorp.me' and 'mne.asseco.android.ae.nlbmne' identify Asseco as NLB Montenegro's digital-banking vendor; 'com.payten.nlb.podgorica' identifies Payten as its SmartPOS vendor. A cheap, high-confidence vendor-to-bank mapping that no notice publishes.

source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore – Finansijski izvještaji banaka + annual report
why_relevant: Central repository of every licensed bank's financial statements; notes to accounts disclose intangible assets, software additions and 'nematerijalna ulaganja' — the auditable version of IT capex. Also confirms the exact licensed-institution population for the actor map.

source_name: Banking Fraud Summit Montenegro (Podgorica) – agenda and sponsor list
why_relevant: Recurring Podgorica banking event (18th edition announced for 22 Oct 2026) whose sponsor and speaker lists identify fraud/AML/card-security vendors targeting Montenegrin banks — a niche the notice-bearing cells rarely capture early.

source_name: LinkedIn – INFINTECH showcase page and Montenegrin bank/vendor company pages
why_relevant: Bank and vendor LinkedIn pages carry vacancy posts and 'we are implementing X' announcements earlier than corporate sites; the INFINTECH showcase page reposts sponsor announcements. Highest-yield channel for the cell's hiring signal but the most access-constrained.

source_name: Porto Montenegro events calendar (INFINTECH host venue)
why_relevant: Venue-side listing confirms event dates and sometimes lists partner organisations before the event's own site updates — a secondary confirmation channel for the conference-signal stream.

source_name: Consolidated text of the Zakon o javnim nabavkama (Sl. list CG 074/19, 003/23, 011/23) - PDF on ujn.gov.me
why_relevant: The operative statute itself: defines contracting authorities, thresholds triggering publication, procedure types, and the mandate for the electronic procurement system. Baseline document against which every future amendment (committed for Q2 2026) must be diffed.

source_name: EUME / Kancelarija za evropske integracije Crne Gore - Chapter 5 (Javne nabavke) accession pages
why_relevant: Publishes chapter-by-chapter accession material and closing-benchmark news. Confirmed reporting that Montenegro met the Chapter 5 closing benchmarks, with binding commitments to amend the Law on Public Procurement and the anti-corruption law by Q2 2026 and to add a red-flag system to the e-procurement platform - i.e. a dated forecast of framework change.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore - e-invoicing (e-fakture) programme
why_relevant: Owner of the mandatory e-invoicing rollout: Montenegro signed an agreement with Serbia's MoF for a free licence to Serbia's centralised e-invoice platform, with B2G/B2B phasing discussed for 2025-2026. A mandatory e-invoicing regime is itself a generator of payments-adjacent tenders and changes obligations on every supplier to the state.

source_name: PropisiNet.me - Svi propisi Crne Gore online
why_relevant: Second commercial consolidator of Montenegrin legislation; useful cross-check when one database lags after an amendment, and it also carries adjacent acts (advokatska tarifa, administrative procedure) that bear on remedies costs.

source_name: CMS Expert Guide to public procurement - Montenegro chapter
why_relevant: Law-firm practice commentary structured around exactly the variables this cell tracks: where notices must be published, value thresholds (states EUR 25,000 supplies/services, EUR 30,000 works), procedure types, appeal deadlines and fees, and whether e-procurement is mandatory. Authored by CMS lawyers with Podgorica/Belgrade coverage. NOTE: the version read appears partly out of date (refers to a 'State Commission for Control of Public Procurements' and voluntary e-procurement), so treat its figures as needing verification against the 2019/2023 law - which is itself a useful signal of how fast law-firm content ages.

source_name: OECD/SIGMA - Central public procurement institutions in the Western Balkans
why_relevant: Directly addresses central purchasing bodies - the structural change most likely to concentrate future payments-hardware and IT procurement into a few large framework agreements, changing where and how such tenders appear.

source_name: CEFTA Transparency Pack - Public Procurement country pages
why_relevant: Regional trade-facilitation portal that indexes each CEFTA party's procurement legal framework and publication portals in one place - a compact pointer for cross-checking Montenegro's stated rules against neighbours, and for discovering portals not linked from national sites.

source_name: Pagero / Thomson Reuters - Montenegro e-invoicing compliance tracker
why_relevant: Commercial compliance tracker that dates e-invoicing mandates country by country. For ME it records the Serbian-platform licence route and expected B2G/B2B phasing - the cleanest running timeline of an obligation that will drive integration and payments tenders.

source_name: dddInvoices - Electronic Fiscalization and E-Invoicing in Montenegro
why_relevant: Second independent commercial tracker covering both Montenegrin electronic fiscalisation (already live) and the pending e-invoicing mandate; useful to triangulate dates and to understand how fiscalisation infrastructure interacts with any B2G e-invoicing obligation.

source_name: Dan, Portal Analitika, Standard - ME press on Chapter 5 and procurement reform
why_relevant: Cluster of Montenegrin outlets that covered the Chapter 5 closing-benchmark decision. Together they provide redundancy in local-language monitoring and often quote officials on timelines for the Q2 2026 law amendments.

source_name: CRNVO - NGO-hosted archive of the Law on Public Procurement
why_relevant: NGO resource centre mirror of the promulgated law text; useful as a redundancy copy of historical versions when official pages are reorganised (a recurring problem with gov.me migrations).
